transcript.text:
Excellent work, everyone. Let me pull this all together and lay out where we stand and what we need to do.

First, on the litigation front — Thomas, your demand-futility analysis is our primary lever. Five of seven directors independent at time of demand gives us a strong motion-to-dismiss posture at the pleading stage. Get me that memorandum by end of day tomorrow, and I agree with your framing point — any governance reforms must be positioned as voluntary improvements, not concessions of oversight deficiencies, so they don't undercut the demand-futility argument. That's a critical coordination point between litigation and governance.

Second, Nadia — update the board-resolution checklist immediately and circulate the bylaw provision to the team today. We need to identify the three independent directors who would serve on the special committee now, so we're ready to move if our response includes any governance undertakings. That committee process is our governance gate.

Third, Victor — the 10-business-day notice clock is the most urgent item. Get me the precise trigger date and the exact notice format requirements by end of day today. In the meantime, your instruction is clear: no one on this team engages in any discussions with the plaintiff or opposing counsel that could be construed as an admission or settlement overture until we have written carrier consent. Let's plan to send notice as soon as you confirm the trigger date.

Fourth, Maya — I agree with your concern. The board chair's instruction — governance reforms only, no monetary payment, no admission — is directionally consistent with our demand-futility strategy, but it needs to be a formal board position, not just the chair's personal view. Go back to the chair, confirm whether this reflects a formal board position or the chair's individual stance, and if it's not formal, get it on the board agenda promptly. The full board needs to adopt this posture so we're building our response on solid ground.

Let me be clear about the interaction here: the board's no-admission, no-payment position actually simplifies our insurance posture — Victor, if we're not making any admission or entering any settlement, the carrier consent requirement may not be triggered — but we still need to give notice within 10 business days regardless. And any governance reforms we propose will need to clear Nadia's special committee of three independent directors and be framed consistently with Thomas's demand-futility strategy.

So our action items are: Thomas — memorandum by end of day tomorrow. Nadia — checklist updated, bylaw circulated, and three independent directors identified — today. Victor — trigger date and notice format by end of day today. Maya — confirm whether the chair's instruction is a formal board position, and if not, get it on the board agenda. I want all of these items resolved before I authorize any response to the complaint. We have four weeks, but the insurance clock is the tightest constraint, and we need to move on all fronts in parallel.
